# Verification map

<!-- Generated by `make verification` from the tests, /docs/requirements.md, /docs/unsupported.md, and the simulator's kill matrix. Do not edit it by hand. -->

This document maps every requirement of maragudb to the tests that verify it. The IDs come from the documents that state the requirements: `AC-` marks an acceptance criterion and `INV-` a key invariant in [requirements.md](requirements.md), `UNS-` a class of Postgres statements that maragudb rejects with `ErrUnsupported` in [unsupported.md](unsupported.md), and `DEV-` a remaining difference from Postgres, listed there too. `MUT-` marks a mutant, a deliberate bug the checkers must catch, and `STATE-` an interesting state the simulator must reach.

The tests declare what they verify, and `make verification` generates this document from those declarations and the documents above. A test fails if the generated text differs from this file, if an ID has no test, or if a test names an ID that does not exist, so the map cannot go stale.

Each entry names the test's package, the test's name, and what the test asserts, in one line. The numbers behind each run, such as seeds, anomalies, and reached-state counts, are in the verification report on the summary page of every [CI run](https://github.com/maragudk/maragudb/actions/workflows/ci.yml).

## At a glance

- 36 acceptance criteria (`AC-`), 28 key invariants (`INV-`), 31 classes of unsupported statements (`UNS-`), and 1 remaining differences from Postgres (`DEV-`), each verified by at least one test.
- 31 mutants (`MUT-`), deliberate bugs, of which 29 are detected by the simulator's checkers within 20 seeds.
- 29 interesting states (`STATE-`) that the simulator's fixed corpus must reach.
- 299 declarations of coverage in the tests.

## Acceptance criteria

### `AC-1.1`

> Serializability under faults: errors

- `internal/engine` `TestDB_ReadRetries/retries_a_block_read_that_fails_transiently,_backing_off_on_the_clock`: a block read that fails transiently is retried with backoff on the clock and succeeds
- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/a_commit_whose_manifest_write_failed_before_applying_is_retried_and_succeeds`: a manifest write that failed before applying is retried and the commit succeeds
- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Faults/errors_are_not_applied`: an injected error fails the write and leaves the store unchanged
- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Unavailable/an_outage_refuses_every_request_until_it_ends,_without_crashing_the_process`: an outage fails every request until it ends, while the process keeps running
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `AC-1.2`

> Serializability under faults: latency

- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Faults/latency_advances_the_virtual_clock`: injected latency advances the virtual clock, by at most the maximum latency
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `AC-1.3`

> Serializability under faults: lost acknowledgements, where the write succeeded but the response was lost

- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/a_commit_whose_manifest_write_lost_its_acknowledgement_is_reported_as_success_exactly_once`: a commit whose manifest write lost its acknowledgement is resolved as landed, reported once, and visible
- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/a_lost_acknowledgement_followed_by_another_process's_commit_is_resolved_as_success`: a lost acknowledgement followed by another process's commit is resolved from the commit records as success
- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Faults/a_lost_ack_hides_a_precondition_failure_too`: a lost acknowledgement also hides a precondition failure, so the client cannot tell what happened
- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Faults/lost_acks_are_applied_but_reported_as_errors`: a lost acknowledgement applies the write and still reports an error
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus reaches every declared state at least once, among them crashes during commits, compactions, and GC passes, lost acknowledgements resolved both ways, unique and foreign key violations that only a concurrent commit causes, disk caches that evict and refuse damaged files, damaged reads from the store refused with ErrCorrupt, and point lookups that skip segments by their key filters and read filter blocks with root blocks

### `AC-1.4`

> Serializability under faults: client crashes at any step, including mid-commit and mid-compaction or mid-GC

- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Faults/a_crashed_process_cannot_make_further_requests`: a crashed process fails every later request, and other processes are unaffected
- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Faults/crashes_happen_both_before_and_after_apply`: over 50 seeds, crashes happen both before and after the write is applied
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus reaches every declared state at least once, among them crashes during commits, compactions, and GC passes, lost acknowledgements resolved both ways, unique and foreign key violations that only a concurrent commit causes, disk caches that evict and refuse damaged files, damaged reads from the store refused with ErrCorrupt, and point lookups that skip segments by their key filters and read filter blocks with root blocks

- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/the_SQL_workloads_exercise_the_same_paths_as_the_engine_workloads`: the SQL corpus exercises commits, conflicts, unknown outcomes, outages, crashes, compactions, and deletes

- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `AC-1.8`

> Serializability under faults: an Elle-style list-append workload, which checks for strict serializability

- `internal/history` `TestCheckListAppend`: the list-append checker accepts serializable histories and rejects stale reads, write skew, lost updates, reads of failed writes, duplicate values, and cycles through real-time edges
- `internal/history` `TestChecks_Properties/accept_every_serial_history`: the checkers accept every generated serial history, so they raise no false alarms
- `internal/history` `TestChecks_Properties/reject_a_serial_history_whose_acknowledged_read_was_truncated_by_one_value`: the checkers reject every generated serial history with one acknowledged read truncated
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `AC-1.9`

> Serializability under faults: Each failure can be reproduced from its seed alone.

- `internal/s3fake` `TestClient_Faults/the_same_seed_produces_the_same_outcomes`: the same seed produces the same fault outcomes, final keys, and virtual time
- `internal/sched` `TestScheduler/produces_the_same_trace_on_every_run`: the scheduler produces the same trace of task steps on every run
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/replay`: a seed in MARAGUDB_SEED replays with a full trace, from make replay; skipped otherwise
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/the_same_seed_produces_the_same_history`: the same seed gives a byte-identical history, final state, and statistics, through the engine and SQL, in every maintenance mode, also for the foreign key workload, whose now() comes from the virtual clock

### `AC-2`

> The checkers can fail. Deliberately broken builds must be detected by criterion 1. Examples: commit without CAS, GC that deletes too early, a cache served without a freshness check. This proves that the tests are not vacuous.

- `internal/history` `TestChecks_Properties/reject_a_serial_history_where_an_acknowledged_append_was_dropped_from_the_final_state`: the checkers reject every generated serial history whose final state lost one acknowledged append
- `internal/history` `TestChecks_Properties/reject_a_serial_history_whose_acknowledged_read_was_truncated_by_one_value`: the checkers reject every generated serial history with one acknowledged read truncated
- `internal/sim` `TestMutants`: every mutant is detected by a checker in at least one simulator configuration, every configuration that cannot detect a mutant says why, and the kill matrix matches its golden file
- `internal/verify` `TestVerification/every_mutant_is_detected_by_the_simulator_or_by_a_targeted_test`: no mutant in the kill matrix goes undetected by both the simulator and the targeted tests
- `internal/verify` `TestVerification/the_verification_map_is_up_to_date`: docs/verification.md equals what the tests and documents generate

- `internal/history` `TestCheckDurability`: the durability checker rejects a missing acknowledged write, an applied failed write, a partially applied unknown transaction, and values in the wrong key or never written
- `internal/history` `TestChecks_Properties/reject_a_serial_history_where_an_acknowledged_append_was_dropped_from_the_final_state`: the checkers reject every generated serial history whose final state lost one acknowledged append
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `AC-3.2`

> Durability and atomicity: An unacknowledged commit is either completely visible or completely invisible, never partial.

- `internal/history` `TestCheckDurability`: the durability checker rejects a missing acknowledged write, an applied failed write, a partially applied unknown transaction, and values in the wrong key or never written
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `AC-4.1`

> Differential testing against Postgres. Hegel generates schemas, data, transactions, and statements as an AST, which is rendered once to Postgres SQL. Both systems run the same text, and the Postgres side runs in Docker.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDifferential/generated_statements_give_the_same_results_on_Postgres_and_maragudb`: hegel-generated schemas, rows, transactions, and statements, written once as Postgres SQL, give the same results, column names, affected-row counts, and transaction states on both sides, ordered exactly when ORDER BY decides the order and as multisets otherwise, and fail on both sides with the same error class, except for statements that maragudb rejects as unsupported, which Postgres skips
- `internal/sql/parser` `TestParse/round_trips_every_statement_through_the_renderer`: every generated statement AST renders to SQL that parses back to the same AST

### `AC-4.2`

> Differential testing against Postgres: When ORDER BY determines the order completely, results must match exactly. Otherwise they must match as multisets.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDifferential/generated_statements_give_the_same_results_on_Postgres_and_maragudb`: hegel-generated schemas, rows, transactions, and statements, written once as Postgres SQL, give the same results, column names, affected-row counts, and transaction states on both sides, ordered exactly when ORDER BY decides the order and as multisets otherwise, and fail on both sides with the same error class, except for statements that maragudb rejects as unsupported, which Postgres skips
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestJoins/joins_as_Postgres_does`: several tables in FROM, CROSS JOIN, [INNER] JOIN with ON and USING, LEFT [OUTER] JOIN with ON and USING, NATURAL joins, self-joins, and parenthesized and nested joins give Postgres's rows and column names, with the columns that USING merges once, of the common type, and those of a LEFT JOIN's right side NULL where it has no row

### `AC-4.3`

> Differential testing against Postgres: Both systems must agree on whether a statement succeeds or fails, and on the error class when both fail. Postgres runs with enable_seqscan = off, so that the differences with a DEV- ID do not show.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCTEs/evaluates_subqueries_in_FROM_and_CTEs_as_Postgres_does,_with_their_names_and_errors`: subqueries in FROM with an alias and names for their columns, and non-recursive CTEs, several of them, a later one reading an earlier one, with names for their columns, read several times or never, and in subqueries, give Postgres's rows, names, and errors, such as 42712 for a CTE named twice and 42P10 for too many column names
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestChecks/names_CHECK_constraints_as_Postgres_does,_and_fails_a_CHECK_as_Postgres_does_when_the_table_is_created`: CHECK constraints get Postgres's names, after the one column they read or after the table, numbered past the names of every constraint of every table, they share the names of a table's constraints with its PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints and its NOT NULL constraints, and a CHECK that is not boolean, reads a missing column, or repeats a name fails with the class of Postgres's error
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDefaults/fills_in_defaults_as_Postgres_does,_with_the_same_errors`: a column's DEFAULT is used for a column that an INSERT leaves out, for DEFAULT in VALUES and in SET, and for DEFAULT VALUES, converted to the column's type by assignment, and a DEFAULT that reads a column, has a parameter, has the wrong type, or fails to fold fails as in Postgres
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDifferential/generated_statements_give_the_same_results_on_Postgres_and_maragudb`: hegel-generated schemas, rows, transactions, and statements, written once as Postgres SQL, give the same results, column names, affected-row counts, and transaction states on both sides, ordered exactly when ORDER BY decides the order and as multisets otherwise, and fail on both sides with the same error class, except for statements that maragudb rejects as unsupported, which Postgres skips
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestErrorClasses`: every maragudb error class fails with its mapped SQLSTATE code on Postgres for the same statement
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/creates_and_drops_foreign_keys_as_Postgres_does,_with_the_same_names_and_errors`: FOREIGN KEY and REFERENCES get Postgres's names, reference a primary key or the first unique index on the referenced columns, fail with the class of Postgres's error for a missing table or column, columns without a unique index, a different number of columns, and incompatible types, and DROP TABLE and DROP INDEX of what a foreign key depends on fail with 2BP01
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestGroupBy/groups_by_expressions,_output_positions,_and_output_names,_with_Postgres's_resolution_and_errors`: GROUP BY of expressions, output positions, and names, where a name is a column of FROM before it is an output column's, HAVING with and without GROUP BY, aggregates in ORDER BY, and the grouping errors of Postgres: an ungrouped column (42803) unless the GROUP BY has the primary key of its table, nested aggregates and aggregates in WHERE, JOIN conditions, GROUP BY, LIMIT, VALUES, and UPDATE (42803), positions out of range (42P10), constants (42601), and ambiguous names (42702)
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexConditions/evaluates_the_other_conditions_only_on_the_rows_that_the_primary_key_conditions_select,_as_Postgres_does_with_an_index_scan`: with sequential scans off, Postgres evaluates the other WHERE conditions only on the rows that the conditions on the primary key index select: comparisons and IN of constants on any key column, a boolean key column, and key equalities implied by equalities with a constant; maragudb accepts such statements and gives the same results
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexConditions/takes_the_index_conditions_out_of_an_OR_as_Postgres_does_when_it_drops_constants_and_common_conditions_from_the_OR`: in a WHERE clause, Postgres drops the arguments of an OR that are FALSE or NULL constants and takes the conditions common to every argument out of the OR, which can make them index conditions; maragudb does the same and gives the same results
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexPlans/evaluates_the_other_conditions_only_on_the_rows_that_every_index_scan_Postgres_could_pick_skips,_and_otherwise_on_every_row`: with several indexes, a condition that can fail is evaluated on the rows that any index scan Postgres could pick reads: those of each index's certain conditions, and every row when an index without them could serve a condition or ORDER BY; maragudb gives Postgres's result when every such scan agrees, and rejects the statement otherwise
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/names_indexes_as_Postgres_does,_in_the_namespace_of_tables,_with_the_same_errors`: CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX, and UNIQUE constraints name their indexes as Postgres does, tables and indexes share one namespace, and every clash, missing name, and wrong kind of relation fails with the class of Postgres's error
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestJoins/resolves_aliases_and_qualified_names_as_Postgres_does,_with_the_same_errors`: table aliases with and without AS, names for the columns of a table, qualified names, t.*, and a name alone resolve as in Postgres, and an ambiguous name (42702), a missing or hidden FROM entry (42P01), a table named twice (42712), a missing column (42703), and too many column names (42P10) fail with the class of Postgres's error
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestRowOrder/reports_the_error_of_rows_that_fail_with_one_class_in_any_order,_and_rejects_rows_that_fail_with_different_classes_where_Postgres_may_read_them_in_another_order_than_the_key`: a SELECT on one table whose rows fail with different classes of error is rejected when a sort key in descending order lets Postgres scan the primary key backward, or its rows come from a subquery in FROM or a CTE, and fails with the class of every failing row when they agree, or with the class of the first row in key order when Postgres reads them in key order, and two WHERE conditions that fail on one row with different classes are rejected
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestRunner_Run/accepts_different_errors_that_agree_once_Postgres_visits_the_rows_in_key_order_instead_of_the_order_of_an_index`: when Postgres reads the rows through an index in the order of its entries and reports another row's error than maragudb, which reads them in key order, the rerun in key order marks the other indexes invalid, so that Postgres agrees
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestRunner_Run/reports_errors_of_different_classes_as_a_mismatch`: a statement that fails on both sides for different reasons is a mismatch
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestSubqueries/fails_a_scalar_subquery_with_more_than_one_row_with_21000,_and_a_subquery_with_the_wrong_number_of_columns_as_Postgres_does`: a scalar subquery with more than one row fails with 21000 where every plan evaluates it, and a subquery with several columns fails with 42601
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestSubqueryNames/resolves_names_in_the_query_of_a_subquery_first_and_then_in_the_queries_around_it,_as_Postgres_does,_with_the_same_errors`: a name in a subquery resolves in its own FROM first and then in the queries around it, from the nearest out, a qualified name by the nearest table of that name, with 42702 for an ambiguous name at the nearest level that has it, 42703 and 42P01 when no level has it, and 42803 for an ungrouped column of a grouped query around

### `AC-4.4`

> Differential testing against Postgres: Every class of statement that maragudb rejects with ErrUnsupported is listed in docs/unsupported.md with a stable UNS- ID and a test that shows Postgres accepting it and maragudb rejecting it. Any remaining difference from Postgres is listed there too, with a DEV- ID and its own test.

- `internal/verify` `TestVerification/every_requirement_and_unsupported_statement_is_verified_by_a_test,_and_every_test_names_IDs_that_exist`: every acceptance criterion, invariant, class of unsupported statements, and remaining difference has a verifying test, and no test declares an unknown ID
- `internal/verify` `TestVerification/the_verification_map_is_up_to_date`: docs/verification.md equals what the tests and documents generate

### `AC-4.5`

> Differential testing against Postgres: A statement that maragudb rejects with ErrUnsupported is not run on Postgres, and the harness counts it as rejected. With a fixed seed, at least 70% of the generated statements run on both systems, and the number that do never drops below a committed baseline.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDifferential/the_generator_mostly_produces_SQL_that_maragudb_accepts,_and_no_less_than_the_committed_baseline`: with a fixed seed, at least 70% of the generated statements run on both sides, and no fewer than the baseline in testdata/ratchet.json
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestRunner_Run/skips_a_rejected_statement_on_Postgres,_and_aborts_the_transaction_there_instead`: a statement that maragudb rejects as unsupported is counted as rejected and not run on Postgres, and inside a transaction both transactions end up aborted

### `AC-4.6`

> Differential testing against Postgres: The SQLite sqllogictest corpus runs live on both systems under the same rules, with Postgres as the only oracle. A fixed set of its files runs in make test and the full corpus in make soak. For each file, the number of statements that run on both systems never drops below a committed baseline.

- `internal/sqllogictest` `TestCorpus/the_statements_of_the_corpus_give_the_same_results_on_Postgres_and_maragudb,_and_no_file_executes_fewer_of_them_than_its_baseline`: the SQLite sqllogictest corpus, rewritten once and run as the same text on both sides, gives the same results, column names, affected-row counts, and error classes on Postgres and maragudb, except for statements that maragudb rejects as unsupported, and every file executes at least its committed baseline of statements on both sides

### `AC-5.1`

> S3 request budgets: A commit uses O(1) PUTs, independent of database size.

- `.` `TestMaintenance/keeps_the_commit_and_warm-read_budgets_in_steady_state`: with background maintenance, an INSERT and a warm SELECT keep their request budgets
- `.` `TestRequestBudgets/an_autocommit_INSERT_makes_one_conditional_GET_and_two_PUTs_regardless_of_database_size`: an autocommit INSERT makes one conditional GET and two PUTs at every database size, after many commits with the merges of the tiers, and after a compaction of every segment
- `.` `TestRequestBudgets_ForeignKeys/an_insert_of_a_row_with_a_foreign_key_adds_no_request_with_a_warm_cache,_and_a_logarithmic_number_of_GETs_with_a_cold_one`: an autocommit INSERT of a row that references a parent makes one conditional GET and two PUTs with a warm cache at every database size, and with a cold cache one descent of the tree of every segment each for the table definitions, the duplicate key check, and the lookup of the parent, after many commits with the merges of the tiers, and after a compaction of every segment; after the many commits, at most one and a half times the GETs of the compacted database, or two more, at every size up to 100,000 rows
- `.` `TestRequestBudgets_Indexes/a_commit_that_changes_indexed_columns_makes_one_conditional_GET_and_two_PUTs_regardless_of_database_size`: an autocommit UPDATE that changes the columns of two indexes, and so deletes and writes entries of both, makes one conditional GET and two PUTs at every database size
- `internal/engine` `TestRequestBudgets/a_commit_uses_two_PUTs_and_one_GET_regardless_of_database_size`: a commit makes one conditional GET, one PUT, and one conditional PUT at 100 to 100,000 keys

### `AC-5.2`

> S3 request budgets: A transaction with a warm cache uses one conditional GET (or HEAD) for the freshness check, plus nothing else for cached data, also for the key filters of segments.

- `.` `TestMaintenance/keeps_the_commit_and_warm-read_budgets_in_steady_state`: with background maintenance, an INSERT and a warm SELECT keep their request budgets
- `.` `TestRequestBudgets/a_SELECT_by_primary_key_with_a_warm_cache_makes_exactly_one_conditional_GET`: a SELECT by primary key with a warm cache makes exactly one conditional GET
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_KeyFilters/a_warm_cache_adds_no_GET_for_filters,_and_the_disk_cache_holds_filter_blocks_as_it_holds_other_blocks`: a point lookup with a warm memory cache makes only the freshness read, and one with a warm disk cache reads the filter blocks from it, so that a segment whose filter does not hold the key costs no GET
- `internal/engine` `TestRequestBudgets/a_transaction_with_a_warm_cache_uses_one_conditional_GET_and_nothing_else`: a read-only transaction with a warm cache makes exactly one conditional GET at 100 to 10,000 keys

### `AC-5.3`

> S3 request budgets: A point lookup with a cold cache uses at most one GET per tree level of each live segment, so O(log n) GETs per segment, and compaction keeps O(log n) live segments. A live segment whose key filter shows that it does not hold the key costs at most one GET, and none when the manifest holds the filter. The lookup stays within the tiered bound.

- `.` `TestRequestBudgets/a_SELECT_by_primary_key_with_a_cold_cache_makes_a_logarithmic_number_of_GETs`: a SELECT by primary key with a cold cache makes at most one GET per tree level of every segment for the table definition and the row, after many commits with the merges of the tiers, which leave fewer than four segments per tier, and one GET per tree level after a compaction of every segment; after the many commits, at most one and a half times the GETs of the compacted database, or two more, at every size up to 100,000 rows
- `.` `TestRequestBudgets/an_autocommit_INSERT_makes_one_conditional_GET_and_two_PUTs_regardless_of_database_size`: an autocommit INSERT with a cold cache makes at most one GET per tree level of every segment for the table definition and the duplicate key check, after many commits with the merges of the tiers, which leave fewer than four segments per tier, and after a compaction of every segment
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_KeyFilters/a_cold_point_lookup_makes_no_GET_for_a_segment_whose_filter_in_the_manifest_does_not_hold_the_key,_and_one_for_a_segment_whose_filter_block_does_not`: a cold point lookup of a key of the oldest segment alone makes the GETs of a descent of the oldest segment, one GET for the root and filter blocks of a newer segment whose filter block does not hold the key, and none for three newer segments whose filters in the manifest do not hold it; without the filters, it descends into every segment
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_KeyFilters/a_lookup_reads_a_filter_block_alone_when_a_scan_put_the_root_block_in_the_cache_without_it,_and_keeps_it`: after a scan cached the root block of a segment but not its filter block, a cold lookup of a key that the segment does not hold makes one GET, for the filter block, and the next one none
- `internal/engine` `TestMaintainer_Compaction/reads_and_writes_a_number_of_bytes_per_committed_byte_that_grows_with_the_logarithm_of_the_size,_while_it_grows_a_database_tenfold`: growing an empty database by commits of ten new keys, an update, and a delete each, with maintenance after every commit, from 300 commits to 3,000, makes compaction read and write at most two bytes more per committed byte for every fourfold of the size, plus two, and leaves fewer than four segments in each tier after every maintenance step
- `internal/engine` `TestMaintainer_Compaction/reads_and_writes_about_as_many_bytes_per_committed_byte_for_the_same_commits_on_a_database_ten_times_as_large`: 1,000 commits on databases of 2,000 and 20,000 keys, with a maintenance step after every commit, leave fewer than four segments in each tier, where a segment counts in the highest tier of itself and the newer segments
- `internal/engine` `TestRequestBudgets/a_point_lookup_with_a_cold_cache_uses_a_logarithmic_number_of_GETs`: a cold point lookup makes one freshness check and at most one GET per tree level, 1 + log16(n), at 100 to 100,000 keys
- `internal/engine` `TestSegment/a_point_lookup_fetches_at_most_one_block_per_tree_level,_logarithmic_in_entry_count`: a point lookup in a random segment fetches at most one block per tree level

### `AC-5.5`

> S3 request budgets: A point lookup through a secondary index with a cold cache uses that budget for the index entry and again for the row. A lookup through a unique index stays within the tiered bound.

- `.` `TestRequestBudgets_Indexes/a_point_lookup_through_a_unique_index_with_a_cold_cache_makes_a_logarithmic_number_of_GETs`: a SELECT by a unique secondary index with a cold cache makes a logarithmic number of GETs: one descent of the tree of every segment each for the table definition, the index entry, and the row, after many commits with the merges of the tiers, which leave fewer than four segments per tier, and after a compaction of every segment; after the many commits, at most one and a half times the GETs of the compacted database, or two more, at every size up to 100,000 rows

### `AC-5.6`

> S3 request budgets: A commit that changes indexed columns still uses O(1) PUTs, independent of database size and of the number of indexes.

- `.` `TestRequestBudgets_Indexes/a_commit_that_changes_indexed_columns_makes_one_conditional_GET_and_two_PUTs_regardless_of_database_size`: an autocommit UPDATE that changes the columns of two indexes, and so deletes and writes entries of both, makes one conditional GET and two PUTs at every database size

### `AC-5.7`

> S3 request budgets: An insert of a row with a foreign key with a warm cache uses no request beyond those of any other commit, and with a cold cache the budget of a point lookup for the referenced row, within the tiered bound.

- `.` `TestRequestBudgets_ForeignKeys/an_insert_of_a_row_with_a_foreign_key_adds_no_request_with_a_warm_cache,_and_a_logarithmic_number_of_GETs_with_a_cold_one`: an autocommit INSERT of a row that references a parent makes one conditional GET and two PUTs with a warm cache at every database size, and with a cold cache one descent of the tree of every segment each for the table definitions, the duplicate key check, and the lookup of the parent, after many commits with the merges of the tiers, and after a compaction of every segment; after the many commits, at most one and a half times the GETs of the compacted database, or two more, at every size up to 100,000 rows

### `AC-5.8`

> S3 request budgets: A join from one row of a table to the rows that reference it, through an index on the referencing columns, with a cold cache uses the budget of a point lookup for each row it reads, within the tiered bound.

- `.` `TestRequestBudgets_Joins/a_join_from_one_parent_row_to_its_children_through_an_index_on_their_foreign_key_makes_a_logarithmic_number_of_GETs_per_row_with_a_cold_cache`: a SELECT that joins one parent row to its children with ON c.pid = p.id, through an index on c (pid), makes with a cold cache one descent of the tree of every segment for each table definition, for the parent, for the index entries, and for each child, at every database size, after many commits with the merges of the tiers, which leave fewer than four segments per tier, and after a compaction of every segment; after the many commits, at most one and a half times the GETs of the compacted database, or two more, at every size up to 100,000 rows

### `AC-5.4`

> S3 request budgets: Latency against Tigris is measured and reported, but it does not gate.

- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Tigris/commits_are_visible_across_processes_and_latencies_are_reported`: on Tigris, commits of one process are visible to another, and commit and read latencies are recorded
- `internal/s3` `TestAWSClient_Tigris/conditional_writes_and_reads_behave_like_the_fake`: on Tigris, If-None-Match, If-Match, conditional and ranged reads, list, and delete behave like the fake, and the PUT ETag equals the GET ETag; latencies are recorded

## Key invariants

### `INV-S3-ONLY`

> maragudb is an embedded Go SQL database. Its only durable state is in S3-compatible object storage.

- `internal/engine` `TestTx_Commit/a_commit_from_another_process_is_visible_to_a_transaction_begun_after_it`: a transaction in another process sees a commit acknowledged before it began, read from the store
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault

### `INV-MULTI-WRITER`

> Many processes can read and write the same database at the same time, with strict serializable ACID transactions.

- `internal/engine` `TestEngine_MatchesModel/transactions_over_several_processes_with_compaction_and_GC_behave_like_a_map`: random transactions over several processes, with compaction and GC, behave like a map
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/every_checker_passes_with_the_lease_working,_disabled,_and_overlapping`: every checker passes with background maintenance under a working lease, without the lease, and with overlapping leases

### `INV-CACHE-LOSS`

> Caches in memory and on local disk are allowed (in the style of turbopuffer), but correctness never depends on them: losing every cache never loses or corrupts data.

- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/never_serves_bytes_that_the_latest_Put_of_a_key_did_not_put,_never_holds_more_than_the_bound,_and_counts_every_file,_through_damage,_restarts,_and_evictions_and_replacements_in_the_middle_of_reads`: random operations, damaged and cut files, restarts with leftover temporary files, and evictions and replacements in the middle of reads never make a disk cache serve other bytes than the latest Put of the key, and its files never exceed the bound and are all counted
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/refuses_every_damaged_file_and_removes_it`: a disk cache file that is empty, truncated at any length, corrupt in any byte, of another key, or of the format without a header is a miss, and leaves the cache
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/serves_a_read_that_an_eviction_overlaps_whole_or_not_at_all`: an eviction of an entry in the middle of its read gives the whole value on a file system that keeps removed files readable, and a miss on one that cuts the read short, never the bytes it cut
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Damage/damaged_bytes_from_the_memory_or_the_disk_cache_are_a_miss,_counted,_and_read_from_the_store`: a block or manifest that a cache returns damaged is refused, counted, and read from the store, which serves the right value
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_KeyFilters/every_key_reads_its_newest_value_and_absent_keys_read_as_absent,_cold,_warm,_and_through_segments_without_filters`: point lookups of every key of a database whose segments have filters in the manifest and filter blocks find the newest value, with a cold cache, a warm one, and after the filters are removed from the manifest as an older version writes it
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Stats/a_stale_disk-cached_manifest_is_refreshed_on_open`: a stale manifest in the disk cache is replaced by the store's newer one on open
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with injected errors, latency, lost acknowledgements, outages, and crashes, finds no anomalies with any checker and exercises every fault
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with disk caches small enough to evict and files that crashes and the disk damage, finds no anomalies, and after every operation of every client the files of its disk cache are within the bound and all counted

### `INV-DISK-CACHE-BOUND`

> The disk cache holds at most a configured number of bytes: the files it holds never exceed that bound by more than one entry, whatever the access pattern and across restarts.

- `.` `TestDiskCache/keeps_the_files_of_the_disk_cache_within_DiskCacheBytes,_and_serves_reads_from_them_after_a_restart`: a database with a disk cache of 64 KiB, which commits and reads many times that, keeps the files of its disk cache within the bound after every statement, and a database opened again on the directory reads from it
- `.` `TestDiskCache/shares_the_disk_cache_of_a_DSN_between_databases_in_one_process,_and_fails_with_ErrDiskCacheInUse_in_another_process`: two databases of one DSN with one DiskCacheDir in one process both work, and another process that opens the DSN with that directory fails with ErrDiskCacheInUse
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/counts_the_files_of_an_earlier_process_at_open,_oldest_written_first,_removes_its_temporary_files,_and_keeps_other_files`: a disk cache counts the files that are in its directory at open, evicts the least recently written of them first, removes leftover temporary files, and evicts down to a lowered bound at open
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/keeps_counting_a_newer_file_of_a_key_when_a_read_of_the_older_one_fails_in_the_middle`: a read that fails because its entry was evicted and put again in the middle of it leaves the new entry in the cache and counted
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/keeps_its_files_within_the_bound_and_recently_used_entries_cached,_through_a_realistic_workload_with_restarts`: a read-through workload of segment blocks with a hot set, commits that rewrite the manifest, merges that make new segments, and restarts fills a disk cache to many times its bound, and after every operation its files are within the bound and all counted, every entry used within the last bound's worth of entries is a hit, and most hot reads hit
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/keeps_its_files_within_the_bound_by_one_entry_under_concurrent_reads_and_writes`: concurrent read-through workloads on one disk cache never make its files exceed the bound by more than one entry, checked after every operation
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/keeps_its_files_within_the_bound_in_a_directory_of_the_operating_system`: the realistic workload on a disk cache directory of the operating system, with restarts that close and open it again, keeps its files within the bound after every operation
- `internal/cache` `TestDisk/never_serves_bytes_that_the_latest_Put_of_a_key_did_not_put,_never_holds_more_than_the_bound,_and_counts_every_file,_through_damage,_restarts,_and_evictions_and_replacements_in_the_middle_of_reads`: random operations, damaged and cut files, restarts with leftover temporary files, and evictions and replacements in the middle of reads never make a disk cache serve other bytes than the latest Put of the key, and its files never exceed the bound and are all counted
- `internal/cache` `TestOpenDir/refuses_a_directory_that_another_process_has_open_until_that_process_ends,_also_by_a_crash,_and_shares_one_within_a_process`: a second process that opens a disk cache directory fails with ErrInUse while the first has it open, and opens it once the first closed it or crashed; within one process, the opens of a directory share one cache
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_KeyFilters/a_warm_cache_adds_no_GET_for_filters,_and_the_disk_cache_holds_filter_blocks_as_it_holds_other_blocks`: a point lookup with a warm memory cache makes only the freshness read, and one with a warm disk cache reads the filter blocks from it, so that a segment whose filter does not hold the key costs no GET
- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with disk caches small enough to evict and files that crashes and the disk damage, finds no anomalies, and after every operation of every client the files of its disk cache are within the bound and all counted

### `INV-DAMAGE-DETECTED`

> Damaged bytes in an object in the store, whether a block of a segment, including the block of its key filter, the manifest, a garbage batch, or a definition in the catalog, give a clear error that wraps ErrCorrupt, and damaged bytes in a cache are never served, but read from the store instead. Damaged bytes never give a panic, a hang, or wrong data.

- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Damage/a_GC_pass_that_reads_a_damaged_garbage_batch_fails_with_ErrCorrupt,_and_a_later_one_succeeds`: a GC pass whose read of a garbage batch gets damaged bytes fails with ErrCorrupt and deletes nothing, and a later pass collects the garbage
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Damage/a_block_read_from_the_store_with_damaged_bytes_fails_with_ErrCorrupt,_is_cached_nowhere,_and_a_later_read_of_whole_bytes_succeeds`: a read of a block whose bytes the store damaged fails with ErrCorrupt and caches nothing, and the next read of whole bytes succeeds
- `internal/engine` `TestDB_Damage/a_manifest_read_from_the_store_with_damaged_bytes_fails_the_transaction_with_ErrCorrupt,_and_a_later_one_succeeds`: a transaction whose freshness read gets a manifest that the store damaged fails with ErrCorrupt, and keeps the manifest it had

### `INV-PLACEHOLDERS`

> API: Placeholders use the $1 style. A parameter has one type for the whole statement: the type of the first context that coerces it, in the order in which Postgres analyzes the statement, and every later reference has that type. A statement that skips a parameter number, or that reads a parameter in no context that gives it a type, fails with ErrType, as Postgres fails with SQLSTATE 42P18. A reference made before the parameter has a type fails with ErrType when a later context coerces it to another type, or when it reads where no type is given, as Postgres fails with 42P08. Where the type would depend on an order that maragudb does not follow, the statement is rejected, as UNS-PARAMETERS lists. A parameter value that Postgres refuses when it reads it is reported after every error of analysis, as in Postgres.

- `.` `TestDB/gives_a_parameter_the_type_of_its_context,_as_Postgres_does`: a string parameter is read like a quoted literal of the type its context gives it, an int64 converts to a double precision, and a conversion that a Postgres driver might make differently is ErrUnsupported
- `.` `TestDB/round_trips_every_type_through_parameters_and_Scan`: every type and NULL round-trips through $1-style parameters and Scan
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestParameters/a_SELECT_whose_parameters_repeat_across_its_clauses_gives_the_same_result_as_Postgres_with_pgx,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn SELECTs on a table that reference parameters in several contexts each, in the output, WHERE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT, with typed contexts, IS NULL, coalesce, CASE, IN, BETWEEN, and comparisons of two parameters, give the same result or error class as Postgres with pgx, which types each parameter at its first context in the order in which it analyzes the clauses, unless maragudb rejects them as unsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestParameters/a_parameter_gets_the_type_of_its_first_context_in_the_order_in_which_Postgres_analyzes_the_statement,_and_later_references_have_that_type`: statements that reference a parameter in several contexts, among them the optional filters k = $1 OR $1 IS NULL, ($1::bigint IS NULL OR k = $1), coalesce($1, k), and k = coalesce($1, k), and references across the WITH clause, FROM and join conditions, the output, WHERE, HAVING, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, OFFSET, LIMIT, subqueries, INSERT rows, and UPDATE SET and WHERE, give Postgres's result, or its error class: 42P08 for a reference made before the parameter has a type that a later context coerces to another type or reads in IS NULL, and the error of a later reference whose context does not take the type
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestParameters/a_parameter_of_every_Go_type_in_every_context_gives_the_same_result_as_Postgres_with_pgx,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn Go values bound as parameters in contexts that infer different types, among them times at and beyond both ends of timestamptz to the nanosecond and strings that are not UTF-8 or hold NUL, give the same result or error class as Postgres with pgx, or fail on both when pgx refuses to encode them, unless maragudb rejects them as unsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestParameters/a_statement_whose_parameters_repeat_in_several_contexts_or_skip_a_number_gives_the_same_result_as_Postgres_with_pgx,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn statements that reference parameters in several contexts each, skip parameter numbers, or put a parameter only where its type is not determined, such as IS NULL and count(), next to analysis and folding errors, give the same result or error class as Postgres with pgx, among them 42P18 for a parameter whose type Postgres cannot determine and the error of the lowest refused value after every analysis error, unless maragudb rejects them as unsupported
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Insert/binds_parameters_of_every_type`: every type binds through a parameter, and a timestamptz keeps microseconds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/gives_parameters_the_type_of_their_context`: a parameter of a Go type other than string converts to the type its context infers, overflows like an integer in an integer context, and is ErrUnsupported where it cannot convert
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/refuses_the_values_of_parameters_that_Postgres_refuses_when_it_reads_them,_after_a_mistake_anywhere_in_the_statement_and_before_a_folding_error`: a time parameter outside 4714-11-24 BC to the end of 294276, after flooring to microseconds, fails with ErrOutOfRange, and a string parameter that is not UTF-8 or holds a NUL fails with ErrInvalidUTF8 in every context, after the errors of analysis and before those of folding, as Postgres reads parameters, and in a transaction it aborts the transaction; the bounds themselves are stored and read back
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/types_a_parameter_at_its_first_context_in_the_order_in_which_Postgres_analyzes_the_statement`: a parameter gets the type of the first context that coerces it in Postgres's order of analysis, later references have that type, which their contexts convert or refuse, and a reference made before then that a later context coerces to another type or reads in IS NULL fails with ErrType

### `INV-PANIC-RECOVERED`

> API: A panic inside a call into the driver is a bug in maragudb, and it never reaches database/sql: the call fails with an error that wraps ErrInternal and holds the panic's value, the stack goes to the logger, and the connection is discarded. A recovered panic never makes database/sql run a statement again, and a transaction in which a call panicked never commits.

- `.` `TestDriverOptions/recover_a_panic_in_a_driver_call_as_ErrInternal,_log_it_with_its_stack,_and_run_a_write_that_panicked_after_its_commit_once`: through the public driver's options, an UPDATE outside a transaction that panics after its commit fails with ErrInternal and not driver.ErrBadConn, Options.Logger gets the panic with its stack at the error level, and the update lands once
- `internal/sim` `TestRun_panic/a_panic_in_the_SQL_layer_fails_the_run_at_once_with_the_panic's_value_and_stack,_instead_of_hanging_it_in_database/sql`: the simulator's SQL clients go through the driver's recovery of panics, which ends every call that panicked with an error, so that the task fails the run with the panic instead of hanging in database/sql
- `internal/sqldriver` `TestDriver_panics/a_connection_from_Driver.Open_whose_transaction_panicked_closes_its_connector_and_the_maintenance_with_it`: a connection that Driver.Open opened, broken by a panic in a statement of its transaction, closes its connector when it closes, so that background maintenance stops
- `internal/sqldriver` `TestDriver_panics/a_panic_in_a_statement_of_a_transaction_fails_it_with_ErrInternal,_logs_the_stack,_rolls_the_transaction_back_at_once,_and_the_next_statement_runs_on_a_new_connection`: a panic in a statement of a transaction fails it with an error that wraps ErrInternal and names the panic, the log gets the stack, OnPanic sees it, a deferred rollback returns at once, and the next statement runs on a new connection
- `internal/sqldriver` `TestDriver_panics/a_panic_while_a_connection_opens_fails_it_with_ErrInternal_and_leaves_the_connector_usable`: a panic in opening the engine for a connection fails the ping with an error that wraps ErrInternal, and a second ping fails the same way instead of hanging
- `internal/sqldriver` `TestDriver_panics/a_statement_outside_a_transaction_that_panics_after_its_commit_runs_once,_and_database/sql_does_not_run_it_again`: an UPDATE outside a transaction, plain and prepared, that panics after its commit fails with an error that wraps ErrInternal and not driver.ErrBadConn, and its increment lands exactly once
- `internal/sqldriver` `TestDriver_panics/a_transaction_in_which_a_statement_panicked_rolls_back_on_commit,_and_the_commit_fails_with_ErrInternal`: a transaction whose statement panicked after it wrote a row fails its commit with an error that wraps ErrInternal, and the row is not there

### `INV-MAINTENANCE-PANIC`

> API: A panic in background maintenance, which is a bug in maragudb or in the object store, never ends the process either: the maintenance step recovers it, logs its value and stack at the error level, and maintenance tries again from a clean state after a wait that doubles with every panic in a row, up to a cap. Meanwhile reads and writes keep working, the store stays correct wherever the step stopped, maintenance makes progress again once the panic stops, and closing the database stops maintenance promptly, also while it waits.

- `.` `TestMaintenance/survives_a_panic_of_the_store_in_the_middle_of_a_compaction:_the_database_keeps_answering,_the_log_has_the_panic_with_its_stack,_maintenance_backs_off_and_then_compacts_once_the_panic_stops,_and_closing_the_database_while_it_backs_off_stops_it_at_once`: through the public driver, a panic of the store in the middle of a background compaction leaves the process running and the database answering reads and writes, Options.Logger gets the panic with its stack at the error level once, maintenance does nothing for the backoff and compacts after it once the panic stopped, and closing the database while maintenance backs off returns without waiting and stops the goroutine
- `internal/engine` `TestMaintainer_Panics/a_panic_between_the_segment_write_and_the_manifest_write_of_a_compaction,_and_one_in_the_middle_of_garbage_collection,_lose_nothing,_and_garbage_collection_then_deletes_everything_they_left_behind`: a maintenance step that panics after the write of its merged segment, or after garbage collection deleted some garbage, leaves every value readable, and later steps collect everything the panicked steps left behind
- `internal/engine` `TestMaintainer_Panics/recovers_a_panic_in_the_middle_of_a_compaction,_logs_it_with_its_stack,_backs_off_with_a_doubling_wait_up_to_the_cap_while_reads_and_writes_go_on,_and_compacts_once_the_panic_stops`: a maintenance step recovers a panic of the store in the middle of a compaction, logs its value and stack at the error level, does nothing until a backoff that doubles up to its cap has passed, keeps reads and writes working, and compacts once the panic stops, with every value kept
- `internal/sim` `TestClient_maintenancePanicked/counts_the_panic_that_MaintenancePanics_injects,_and_records_any_other_panic,_so_that_the_run_fails_with_it`: the simulator expects only the panic that the fault injection of maintenance panics with, and fails a run with the value and the stack of any other panic that a maintenance step recovered
- `internal/sim` `TestRun_maintenancePanics/panics_that_MaintenancePanics_injects_in_the_middle_of_the_clients'_compactions_and_GC_passes_are_recovered,_every_checker_passes,_and_maintenance_resumes_after_each_backoff`: with panics injected at points the seed picks in the middle of the clients' compactions and GC passes, in every workload, through the engine and SQL, in every maintenance mode, with crashes and with maintainers, every checker passes, steps back off after a panic, and maintenance changes the database again after it

### `INV-PG-SUBSET`

> SQL flavor: a strict subset of Postgres 18. The same SQL text runs on both, and for every statement that maragudb accepts, the result is identical to Postgres: rows, values, column names, affected-row counts, and transaction state. When Postgres fails a statement, maragudb fails it too, with the same error class wherever the error does not depend on evaluation order or physical row order. Statement text that is not valid UTF-8, or that holds a NUL byte, fails with ErrInvalidUTF8 before it is parsed. The only exceptions are the differences that docs/unsupported.md lists with a DEV- ID, an example, and a test each. There is one: DEV-20, where Postgres scans the whole table and fails on a row that the primary key condition does not select, and maragudb does not fail.

- `.` `TestTx/a_statement_that_does_not_parse_aborts_the_transaction,_as_in_Postgres`: a syntax error or an unsupported statement in an explicit transaction aborts it, so a later commit rolls everything back
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregatePlans/Postgres_moves_HAVING_into_WHERE,_stops_sorted_grouping_under_LIMIT,_computes_MIN_and_MAX_from_an_index,_and_adds_floats_in_the_order_of_its_plan`: EXPLAIN and the outcomes on Postgres 18 with sequential scans off show that a HAVING condition without aggregates is a condition of the scan, that sorted grouping under a LIMIT stops reading rows and succeeds where the whole query fails, that MIN and MAX read the first row of an index that passes WHERE and succeed where COUNT fails, that grouping is hashed or sorted by enable_hashagg and enable_sort, and that the SUM of the same floats depends on the order of the rows
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregatePlans/rejects_an_aggregate_whose_result_or_error_depends_on_the_plan,_and_accepts_it_otherwise`: a SUM or AVG of double precision is accepted only when every order of adding gives the same result, with NaN and infinities, and its overflow is an error only when every order overflows; errors in the arguments of aggregates, in the GROUP BY expressions, and in HAVING are reported when every failing row or group fails with the same class; a HAVING condition without aggregates is a WHERE condition; and MIN and MAX that Postgres can compute from the first row of an index reject a WHERE condition that fails
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregates/compares,_sorts,_casts,_and_outputs_numeric_results_as_Postgres_does`: the numeric results of SUM and AVG of integers compare with each other, with integers, and with floats through Postgres's implicit casts, sort, take part in DISTINCT, IS NULL, CASE, COALESCE, NULLIF, and ||, and cast to bigint with rounding half away from zero and overflow errors, to double precision, and to text, while functions of them are rejected
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregates/computes_COUNT,_SUM,_AVG,_MIN,_and_MAX_as_Postgres_does,_with_numeric_results_for_SUM_and_AVG_of_integers`: COUNT(*), COUNT(x), SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX, also with DISTINCT, over bigint, integer, double precision, text, bytea, timestamptz, and NULLs give Postgres's values and types: SUM of integer is bigint, SUM of bigint and AVG of integers are numeric with Postgres's scale, and MIN and MAX of text compare by byte order
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregates/computes_arithmetic_on_numeric_results_with_Postgres's_values,_scales,_and_errors`: unary minus and plus and +, -, *, /, and % on the numeric results of SUM and AVG of integers, with each other and with integer and bigint operands, give Postgres's values and scales, division by zero (22012), and out of range errors (22003), and their results compare, sort, group, and cast as other numerics; with a double precision operand the numeric converts to double precision
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregates/divides_numerics_to_Postgres's_scale_of_at_most_1000_digits,_multiplies_to_at_most_16383,_and_converts_tiny_and_huge_numerics_to_double_precision_with_Postgres's_out_of_range_errors`: repeated division and multiplication of numeric aggregate results give Postgres's text at the limits of scale, a quotient of scale 1000 and a product rounded half away from zero to scale 16383, and a numeric that rounds to zero or infinity as double precision fails with 22003
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCTEs/evaluates_subqueries_in_FROM_and_CTEs_as_Postgres_does,_with_their_names_and_errors`: subqueries in FROM with an alias and names for their columns, and non-recursive CTEs, several of them, a later one reading an earlier one, with names for their columns, read several times or never, and in subqueries, give Postgres's rows, names, and errors, such as 42712 for a CTE named twice and 42P10 for too many column names
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCasts/every_value_casts_to_every_type_the_same_as_Postgres,_or_is_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn values of every supported type, and integer and numeric literals, cast to every supported type and back to text with the same result or error class as Postgres, unless maragudb rejects the cast as unsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestCasts/text_casts_to_every_type,_and_back_to_text,_the_same_as_Postgres,_or_are_rejected_as_unsupported`: hegel-drawn text near valid input for bigint, double precision, boolean, bytea, and timestamptz casts to the type and back to text with the same result or the same error class as Postgres, unless maragudb rejects it as unsupported

### `INV-UNSUPPORTED`

> SQL flavor: maragudb is stricter than Postgres only through ErrUnsupported, SQLSTATE 0A000 (feature_not_supported), whose message says what is unsupported and, where possible, what to write instead. Every class of statement it rejects is listed in docs/unsupported.md.

- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/rejects_what_Postgres_accepts_only_with_ErrUnsupported`: the numeric type, bit strings, non-ISO timestamps, LIKE on bytea, and the other rejections of accepted Postgres SQL are ErrUnsupported with a hint

### `INV-INT-OVERFLOW`

> Types: bigint int8 64-bit integer. Overflow is an error.

- `.` `TestDB/reports_statement_errors_with_errors.Is`: statement errors, including int overflow as ErrOutOfRange, are detectable with errors.Is
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/reports_evaluation_errors_like_Postgres`: integer and bigint overflow in +, -, *, /, unary minus, and abs is ErrOutOfRange, at 32 bits for integer literals, among the other evaluation errors

### `INV-TYPES`

> Types: As in Postgres, an integer literal that fits in 32 bits has type integer, and arithmetic on it overflows at 32 bits; integer itself is not a column type. Postgres's numeric is the type of SUM of bigint and of AVG of integers, and of arithmetic on those results with each other and with integers and bigints, and of nothing else: it holds their results with the digits and scale that Postgres gives them, which reach Go as text. NULL is supported.

### `INV-INDEX-CONSISTENT`

> After any committed history, every index holds exactly the entries derived from its table's rows.

- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_IndexesMatchModel/random_writes_on_a_table_with_indexes_match_a_model,_and_every_index_matches_its_table_after_every_statement`: random inserts, updates, deletes, and index creations and drops on a table with unique and other indexes give the rows and the unique violations of a model, the indexes match the table after every statement, and lookups through every index return the rows of the model
- `internal/sql/value` `TestEncodeIndexKey/byte_order_of_composite_index_keys_equals_the_order_of_every_column_with_its_direction_and_NULL_placement`: the index key encoding sorts composite keys of every type, ascending or descending, with NULLs first or last, in the order Postgres sorts the index

- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Unique/rejects_a_row_whose_values_another_row_has,_in_one_statement_or_across_statements,_and_allows_NULLs`: inserts and updates that would give two rows the same non-NULL values of a unique index fail with ErrDuplicateKey, within one statement, across statements of a transaction, and against committed rows, and NULLs never collide unless NULLS NOT DISTINCT
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Unique/rejects_an_UPDATE_whose_outcome_depends_on_the_order_Postgres_visits_the_rows,_and_fails_a_cycle_of_moves`: an UPDATE whose rows move onto unique values that other rows of it leave is rejected when they form a chain, whose outcome depends on the order, and fails with ErrDuplicateKey when they form a cycle, which fails in every order

### `INV-CHECK`
