- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus, with the foreign key workload under the same faults, finds no reference to a missing row and no row that violates a CHECK in any snapshot a reader saw, and after every run through SQL every foreign key and CHECK of the store holds
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_ForeignKeyCascades/cascades_down_a_chain_of_rows_far_deeper_than_the_stack_would_allow_for_a_recursion_per_row`: an ON DELETE CASCADE down a self-referencing chain of 10,000 rows deletes the whole chain with the stack limited to 1 MiB, so a cascade never recurses once per row
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_ForeignKeysKeepInvariants/random_writes_on_referenced,_referencing,_and_self-referencing_tables_keep_every_foreign_key_and_check,_with_and_without_an_index_on_the_referencing_columns`: random inserts, updates, and deletes, in and out of transactions, on a parent, a child with a random ON DELETE action, and a self-referencing table never leave a row whose foreign key has no parent or a row that violates a CHECK, and a session whose child has an index on its referencing columns gives the same outcomes and rows as one without

## Unsupported statements

### `UNS-NUMERIC`

> The numeric type.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-NUMERIC_numeric_literals_outside_double_precision_and_bigint_contexts,_and_functions_of_numeric`: numeric literals that Postgres keeps as numeric, such as SELECT 1.5 or a literal beyond the bigint range, also next to the numeric results of SUM and AVG and of arithmetic on them, functions of such results, and quoted literals read as numeric are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-TYPES`

> Other types.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-TYPES_other_types`: type names other than the six supported types and their aliases, and type modifiers, are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-TIMESTAMP-INPUT`

> Timestamps outside ISO 8601 and the common era.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-TIMESTAMP-INPUT_timestamps_that_are_not_ISO_8601_or_not_in_the_common_era`: timestamptz text that is not in an ISO 8601 form, special values, named time zones, and instants before year 1 are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-NO-PRIMARY-KEY`

> Tables without a primary key.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-NO-PRIMARY-KEY_tables_without_a_primary_key`: a table without a primary key is rejected, and Postgres accepts it

### `UNS-DDL`

> Other schema statements and constraints.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-DDL_other_schema_statements_and_constraints`: schema statements other than CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, CREATE INDEX, and DROP INDEX, constraints other than PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, DEFAULT, CHECK, and FOREIGN KEY, and a named NOT NULL are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-SEQUENCES`

> Sequences.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-SEQUENCES_sequences,_serial_types,_and_identity_columns`: sequences, the serial types, and identity columns are rejected with a hint, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-DEFAULT`

> A DEFAULT that can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-DEFAULT_a_DEFAULT_that_can_fail`: a DEFAULT whose constant part fails, or that can fail when it is evaluated, is rejected when the table is created, and Postgres accepts the table

### `UNS-CHECK`

> Other forms of CHECK.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-CHECK_other_forms_of_CHECK`: a CHECK with NO INHERIT, NOT VALID, or NOT ENFORCED, or whose constant part fails, is rejected, and Postgres accepts the table

### `UNS-FOREIGN-KEY`

> Other forms of FOREIGN KEY.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-FOREIGN-KEY_other_forms_of_FOREIGN_KEY`: a foreign key with MATCH FULL, ON UPDATE CASCADE, SET NULL, or SET DEFAULT, NOT VALID, NOT ENFORCED, or DEFERRABLE, or on double precision columns, is rejected, and Postgres accepts the table

### `UNS-INDEX`

> Other forms of indexes.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-INDEX_other_forms_of_indexes_and_of_their_constraints`: indexes on expressions, partial indexes, INCLUDE, USING, CONCURRENTLY, ON ONLY, operator classes, COLLATE, storage parameters, tablespaces, ALTER INDEX, several indexes in one DROP INDEX, and DEFERRABLE and NOT DEFERRABLE constraints are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-STATEMENTS`

> Other statements and transaction modes.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-STATEMENTS_other_statements_and_transaction_modes`: statements other than CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT, and the transaction statements, transaction modes other than SERIALIZABLE, and savepoints are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-CLAUSES`

> Other clauses.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-CLAUSES_other_clauses_of_queries_and_writes`: DISTINCT ON, set operations, also in a subquery, FOR UPDATE, RETURNING, ON CONFLICT, INSERT ... SELECT, an alias in INSERT, UPDATE ... FROM, and DELETE ... USING are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-JOINS`

> Other forms of FROM and of names.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-JOINS_other_forms_of_FROM_and_of_names`: RIGHT and FULL joins, LATERAL, an alias for a join or for the columns of USING, VALUES and functions in FROM, names with a schema, a reference to a whole row, and a repeated name in the names of a table's columns are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-SUBQUERIES`

> Other forms of subqueries and of WITH.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-SUBQUERIES_other_forms_of_subqueries_and_of_WITH`: ANY, SOME, and ALL, a row on the left of IN, WITH RECURSIVE, MATERIALIZED and NOT MATERIALIZED, a query that writes in WITH, WITH in front of INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE, a subquery in FROM without an alias, a repeated column name in a subquery in FROM or a CTE, an aggregate of the columns of a query around a subquery, t.* of a table of a query around, and a subquery in the list of an IN, in GROUP BY, or in LIMIT or OFFSET are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-AGGREGATES`

> Other aggregates and forms of grouping.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-AGGREGATES_other_aggregates_and_forms_of_grouping`: FILTER, ORDER BY in an aggregate, WITHIN GROUP, GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, CUBE, the empty grouping set, GROUP BY ALL and DISTINCT, and the aggregates other than COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-FUNCTIONS`

> Other functions.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-FUNCTIONS_functions_other_than_the_supported_ones`: functions other than abs, coalesce, length, lower, nullif, upper, now, transaction_timestamp, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, and the aggregates, including window functions, the other clocks, and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP with a precision, are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-OPERATORS`

> Other operators and predicates.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-OPERATORS_other_operators_and_predicates`: operators and predicates other than the supported ones, such as IS DISTINCT FROM, ILIKE, regular expressions, arrays, row constructors, LIKE ... ESCAPE, LIKE on bytea, COLLATE, and AT TIME ZONE, are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-LITERALS`

> Other forms of constants and identifiers.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-LITERALS_other_forms_of_constants_and_identifiers`: escape, bit, national, Unicode, and dollar-quoted string constants, strings continued across lines, and non-ASCII unquoted identifiers are rejected, and Postgres accepts them

### `UNS-PARAMETERS`

> A parameter whose Go value would need a conversion, or whose type depends on an order that maragudb does not follow.

- `.` `TestDB/gives_a_parameter_the_type_of_its_context,_as_Postgres_does`: a string parameter is read like a quoted literal of the type its context gives it, an int64 converts to a double precision, and a conversion that a Postgres driver might make differently is ErrUnsupported
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PARAMETERS_a_parameter_that_ORDER_BY_or_GROUP_BY_may_take_for_an_output_column,_in_contexts_of_different_types`: a parameter that is an output column and that ORDER BY names by the same parameter, or GROUP BY by the output column's alias, where Postgres may take it for the output column, is rejected when its contexts give it different types, and Postgres with pgx accepts it
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PARAMETERS_a_statement_that_fails_before_its_analysis_reaches_references_of_a_parameter_that_Postgres_analyzes_first`: a statement whose analysis fails where maragudb has not analyzed every reference of a repeated parameter that Postgres analyzes before that point, or where the failure has no position in Postgres's order, is rejected, because the types of those references could make Postgres fail first, and Postgres fails it too
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PARAMETERS_parameters_whose_Go_value_needs_a_conversion`: a parameter whose Go value would have to be converted to the type its context infers, such as a float64 used as a bigint, is rejected, and Postgres with pgx accepts it
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/gives_parameters_the_type_of_their_context`: a parameter of a Go type other than string converts to the type its context infers, overflows like an integer in an integer context, and is ErrUnsupported where it cannot convert

### `UNS-LIMIT-ORDER`

> LIMIT and OFFSET without a total order.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-LIMIT-ORDER_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_without_a_total_order`: LIMIT and OFFSET without ORDER BY on every primary key column, or on groups without ORDER BY on every GROUP BY expression, are rejected, because which rows Postgres returns depends on its plan, and Postgres accepts them
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/rejects_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_whose_rows_or_errors_would_depend_on_Postgres's_plan`: LIMIT and OFFSET need an ORDER BY on every primary key column and no expression that can fail, else ErrUnsupported

### `UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-LIMIT`

> LIMIT and OFFSET with an expression that can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregatePlans/Postgres_moves_HAVING_into_WHERE,_stops_sorted_grouping_under_LIMIT,_computes_MIN_and_MAX_from_an_index,_and_adds_floats_in_the_order_of_its_plan`: EXPLAIN and the outcomes on Postgres 18 with sequential scans off show that a HAVING condition without aggregates is a condition of the scan, that sorted grouping under a LIMIT stops reading rows and succeeds where the whole query fails, that MIN and MAX read the first row of an index that passes WHERE and succeed where COUNT fails, that grouping is hashed or sorted by enable_hashagg and enable_sort, and that the SUM of the same floats depends on the order of the rows
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-LIMIT_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_with_an_expression_that_can_fail`: LIMIT and OFFSET with an output, ORDER BY, or WHERE expression that can fail are rejected, because how many rows Postgres evaluates it on depends on its plan, and Postgres accepts them when no row fails
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/rejects_LIMIT_and_OFFSET_whose_rows_or_errors_would_depend_on_Postgres's_plan`: LIMIT and OFFSET need an ORDER BY on every primary key column and no expression that can fail, else ErrUnsupported

### `UNS-FLOAT-SUM`

> A SUM or AVG of double precision whose result depends on the order of the rows.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregatePlans/Postgres_moves_HAVING_into_WHERE,_stops_sorted_grouping_under_LIMIT,_computes_MIN_and_MAX_from_an_index,_and_adds_floats_in_the_order_of_its_plan`: EXPLAIN and the outcomes on Postgres 18 with sequential scans off show that a HAVING condition without aggregates is a condition of the scan, that sorted grouping under a LIMIT stops reading rows and succeeds where the whole query fails, that MIN and MAX read the first row of an index that passes WHERE and succeed where COUNT fails, that grouping is hashed or sorted by enable_hashagg and enable_sort, and that the SUM of the same floats depends on the order of the rows
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-FLOAT-SUM_a_SUM_or_AVG_of_double_precision_whose_result_depends_on_the_order_of_the_rows`: a SUM or AVG of double precision values whose sum, or whether it overflows, depends on the order in which Postgres adds them is rejected, and Postgres accepts it

### `UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-AGGREGATE`

> MIN and MAX that Postgres computes from the first row of an index, with a WHERE condition that fails.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregatePlans/Postgres_moves_HAVING_into_WHERE,_stops_sorted_grouping_under_LIMIT,_computes_MIN_and_MAX_from_an_index,_and_adds_floats_in_the_order_of_its_plan`: EXPLAIN and the outcomes on Postgres 18 with sequential scans off show that a HAVING condition without aggregates is a condition of the scan, that sorted grouping under a LIMIT stops reading rows and succeeds where the whole query fails, that MIN and MAX read the first row of an index that passes WHERE and succeed where COUNT fails, that grouping is hashed or sorted by enable_hashagg and enable_sort, and that the SUM of the same floats depends on the order of the rows
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestAggregatePlans/rejects_an_aggregate_whose_result_or_error_depends_on_the_plan,_and_accepts_it_otherwise`: a SUM or AVG of double precision is accepted only when every order of adding gives the same result, with NaN and infinities, and its overflow is an error only when every order overflows; errors in the arguments of aggregates, in the GROUP BY expressions, and in HAVING are reported when every failing row or group fails with the same class; a HAVING condition without aggregates is a WHERE condition; and MIN and MAX that Postgres can compute from the first row of an index reject a WHERE condition that fails
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-AGGREGATE_MIN_and_MAX_that_Postgres_can_compute_from_the_first_row_of_an_index,_with_a_WHERE_condition_that_fails`: a SELECT on one table without GROUP BY whose aggregates are all MIN and MAX, with a WHERE condition that fails on a row, is rejected, because Postgres can read only the first row of an index that passes the condition, and Postgres accepts it when that row comes first

### `UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-WHERE`

> A LIKE on an indexed column whose pattern can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-WHERE_a_LIKE_on_an_indexed_column_whose_pattern_can_fail`: a LIKE on a column of the primary key or of another index whose pattern can fail is rejected, because Postgres scans the index for its prefix and evaluates it only on those rows, and Postgres accepts it when no row there fails
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/accepts_a_WHERE_clause_only_when_its_outcome_is_the_same_in_every_order_Postgres_could_pick_on_the_rows_its_primary_key_index_selects`: a WHERE clause whose outcome on a row depends on the order Postgres evaluates its conditions in, including the equalities its equivalence classes imply, is ErrUnsupported, and so is a LIKE on a key column that can fail; the other conditions are evaluated only on the rows that the primary key conditions select, and every other WHERE clause fails exactly when Postgres fails in every order

### `UNS-ORDER-DEPENDENT-WHERE`

> A condition that fails on a row that another condition rejects.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexPlans/evaluates_the_other_conditions_only_on_the_rows_that_every_index_scan_Postgres_could_pick_skips,_and_otherwise_on_every_row`: with several indexes, a condition that can fail is evaluated on the rows that any index scan Postgres could pick reads: those of each index's certain conditions, and every row when an index without them could serve a condition or ORDER BY; maragudb gives Postgres's result when every such scan agrees, and rejects the statement otherwise
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-ORDER-DEPENDENT-WHERE_a_condition_that_fails_on_a_row_that_another_condition_rejects`: a WHERE clause with a condition that fails on a row that another condition rejects is rejected, because whether Postgres fails depends on the order it picks, and Postgres accepts it in the order it picks here
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/accepts_a_WHERE_clause_only_when_its_outcome_is_the_same_in_every_order_Postgres_could_pick_on_the_rows_its_primary_key_index_selects`: a WHERE clause whose outcome on a row depends on the order Postgres evaluates its conditions in, including the equalities its equivalence classes imply, is ErrUnsupported, and so is a LIKE on a key column that can fail; the other conditions are evaluated only on the rows that the primary key conditions select, and every other WHERE clause fails exactly when Postgres fails in every order

### `UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-JOIN`

> A condition of a join that fails on a row that some plan evaluates it on.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestJoinPlans/rejects_a_join_whose_conditions_fail_on_a_row_or_pair_that_some_plan_evaluates_them_on,_and_accepts_it_otherwise`: a condition of a join that can fail, in WHERE or ON, on one table or several, is evaluated on every row and combination of rows that a plan of Postgres could evaluate it on, also on its sides alone and with NULLs for the right side of a LEFT JOIN, and the statement is rejected when it fails on any, while an output expression that fails is reported when every failing row fails with the same class
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-JOIN_a_condition_of_a_join_that_fails_on_a_row_that_some_plan_evaluates_it_on`: a SELECT on several tables with a condition that fails on a row or a combination of rows that a plan of Postgres could evaluate it on is rejected, because whether Postgres fails depends on its join plan, and Postgres accepts it when its plan does not evaluate the condition there

### `UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-SUBQUERY`

> A subquery whose evaluation fails where one plan evaluates it and another does not.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestSubqueryPlans/rejects_a_subquery_whose_evaluation_fails_where_some_plan_evaluates_it_and_another_does_not,_and_accepts_it_otherwise`: a subquery that can fail is evaluated on every row and in every place that a plan of Postgres could evaluate it, an uncorrelated one in a condition before any row, also one whose references to the query around fold away, the conditions of a correlated EXISTS also without a row of the query around, and a subquery in FROM or a CTE before the statement reads any row, and the statement is rejected when the evaluation fails, while a scalar subquery with more than one row fails with 21000 where every plan evaluates it

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-PLAN-DEPENDENT-SUBQUERY_a_subquery_whose_correlation_a_NULL_conjunct_folds_away`: a scalar subquery whose references to the query around sit in a WHERE that a NULL conjunct decides, which Postgres folds to false and evaluates as an uncorrelated InitPlan before any row, is rejected when it returns more than one row and no row reaches it, where Postgres fails with 21000

### `UNS-DISTINCT-ZERO`

> DISTINCT, GROUP BY, MIN, and MAX of values that are equal but print differently.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestJoins/removes_duplicate_rows_with_DISTINCT_as_Postgres_does`: SELECT DISTINCT keeps one row of every group of rows that are equal as Postgres compares them, NULLs equal to each other and NaN equal to NaN, sorts by ORDER BY items that must be output columns (42P10 otherwise), where constants that Postgres reads into equal values match, such as FALSE and 'no'::boolean, and constants of other types do not, and rejects a group of -0 and 0, whose output depends on the plan

### `UNS-STABLE-CONSTANT`

> A conversion between text and timestamptz that reads no columns and can fail.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-STABLE-CONSTANT_a_conversion_between_text_and_timestamptz_that_reads_no_columns_and_can_fail`: a conversion between text and timestamptz without columns that can fail is rejected, because whether Postgres evaluates it while planning depends on the plan, and Postgres accepts it when it does not fail
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Select/does_not_fold_the_stable_conversions_between_timestamptz_and_text,_as_Postgres_does_not,_and_rejects_one_that_can_fail`: a conversion between timestamptz and text is evaluated when the statement runs, so a CASE does not prune on it and a WHERE condition on it is evaluated once before rows are read, and one without columns that can fail is ErrUnsupported

### `UNS-FOREIGN-KEY-ORDER`

> Foreign key actions whose outcome depends on their order.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestForeignKeys/cascades_through_chains_of_tables_and_trees,_and_rejects_actions_whose_outcome_depends_on_their_order`: ON DELETE CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT go through chains of tables and down self-referencing trees as in Postgres, the rows they change are checked like any other, and a DELETE whose actions could give another outcome in another order is rejected
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-FOREIGN-KEY-ORDER_a_DELETE_whose_foreign_key_actions_depend_on_their_order`: a DELETE whose foreign key actions could write columns that a check reads, or write a table through more than one foreign key, is rejected, and Postgres accepts it when it fires the actions in the right order

### `UNS-KEY-UPDATE-ORDER`

> An UPDATE that moves a row onto a key that another row leaves.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestIndexes/fails_a_cycle_of_unique_values_in_an_UPDATE_as_Postgres_does_in_every_order,_and_rejects_a_chain`: an UPDATE whose rows swap the values of a unique index or of the primary key fails with SQLSTATE 23505 on both, an UPDATE that moves a chain of rows onto the values the next one leaves is rejected, and one that moves rows onto free values succeeds on both
- `internal/pgdiff` `TestUnsupported/UNS-KEY-UPDATE-ORDER_an_UPDATE_that_moves_a_key_onto_one_it_moves_away`: an UPDATE that moves a row onto the primary key, or the values of a unique index, of a row that the same statement moves away is rejected, because Postgres checks the key row by row in the order it visits the rows, and Postgres accepts it when it stores the rows in the right order
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Unique/rejects_an_UPDATE_whose_outcome_depends_on_the_order_Postgres_visits_the_rows,_and_fails_a_cycle_of_moves`: an UPDATE whose rows move onto unique values that other rows of it leave is rejected when they form a chain, whose outcome depends on the order, and fails with ErrDuplicateKey when they form a cycle, which fails in every order
- `internal/sql/exec` `TestSession_Update/moves_rows_when_the_primary_key_changes,_and_rejects_a_move_whose_outcome_depends_on_row_order`: an UPDATE of primary key columns succeeds or fails as in Postgres in every row order, and a chain of rows that move onto keys that other rows move away from is ErrUnsupported, and a cycle of them ErrDuplicateKey

## Remaining differences from Postgres

### `DEV-20`

> A condition that can fail on a row that the primary key does not select.

- `internal/pgdiff` `TestDifferences/DEV-20_Postgres_with_sequential_scans_can_fail_on_a_row_that_the_primary_key_does_not_select`: on a small table with statistics, Postgres in its default configuration scans the whole table and fails on a row that the primary key condition does not select, maragudb evaluates the condition only on the selected rows and succeeds, and Postgres with enable_seqscan=off gives the same result as maragudb

## Mutant kill matrix

Every mutant runs in every simulator configuration below, with seeds 1 to 20, until a checker finds an anomaly. A configuration that never detects a mutant states why it cannot. `make verification` and `make soak` try all 20 seeds in such a configuration, and `make test` seeds 1 to 5.

| Mutant | Detected in | First seed | Checkers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MUT-COMMIT-WITHOUT-CAS` commit without CAS | 9 of 12 configurations | 1 | durability, list-append, real-time order, storage |
| `MUT-GC-IGNORE-GRACE` GC ignoring the grace period | 6 of 12 configurations | 1 | final read, grace period, list-append |
| `MUT-GC-BATCH-OBJECTS-FIRST` garbage batches deleted before their garbage | 6 of 6 configurations | 1 | storage |
| `MUT-GC-SWEEP-SEGMENTS-ONLY` an orphan sweep that misses garbage batches | 6 of 6 configurations | 1 | storage |
| `MUT-GC-CHAIN-FIRST-STAMP` a chain of garbage batches with the stamp of its first batch | 6 of 6 configurations | 3 | grace period |
| `MUT-GC-DELETE-REFERENCED` GC deleting expired garbage that is referenced again | 3 of 6 configurations | 1 | final read, grace period, storage |
| `MUT-COMPACT-NON-ADJACENT` a merge of segments that are not adjacent | 6 of 6 configurations | 1 | bank, durability, index consistency, list-append, unique |
| `MUT-COMPACT-DROP-TOMBSTONES` tombstones dropped in a merge that excludes the oldest segment | 4 of 4 configurations | 1 | durability, foreign key, index consistency, list-append |
| `MUT-COMPACT-REBASE-LOSES-SEGMENT` a rebase that loses a segment added meanwhile | 6 of 6 configurations | 1 | bank, durability, final read, index consistency, list-append, real-time order, unique |
| `MUT-COMPACT-REBASE-ON-COMPACTION` a rebase on another compaction | 2 of 6 configurations | 1 | durability, list-append |
| `MUT-SKIP-FRESHNESS` serving the cache without a freshness check | 9 of 12 configurations | 1 | grace period, list-append, real-time order |
| `MUT-ACK-BEFORE-CONFIRM` acking before the write is confirmed | 9 of 12 configurations | 1 | durability, real-time order, storage |
| `MUT-COMPACTED-AHEAD` the compacted segment ahead of newer ones after a rebase | 5 of 12 configurations | 1 | durability, index consistency, list-append, real-time order |
| `MUT-FRESH-SNAPSHOT` a fresh snapshot per statement | 8 of 8 configurations | 1 | bank, foreign key, index consistency, list-append, workload invariants |
| `MUT-RETRY-UNKNOWN` retrying an autocommit statement after an unknown commit outcome | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | durability, list-append |
| `MUT-INDEX-STALE-DELETE` stale index entries after an UPDATE or DELETE | 6 of 8 configurations | 1 | index consistency |
| `MUT-UNIQUE-NO-CHECK` no unique check | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | index consistency, unique |
| `MUT-UNIQUE-OWN-WRITES` a unique check that misses the statement's own writes | 2 of 8 configurations | 2 | index consistency, unique |
| `MUT-FK-NO-CHILD-CHECK` no check of a referencing row | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | foreign key |
| `MUT-FK-NO-PARENT-CHECK` no check or action on the referencing rows | 2 of 8 configurations | 2 | foreign key |
| `MUT-FK-OWN-WRITES` foreign key lookups that miss the statement's own writes | 2 of 8 configurations | 1 | foreign key |
| `MUT-CHECK-SKIP-UPDATE` CHECK on INSERT only | 2 of 8 configurations | 6 | check constraint |
| `MUT-SUBQUERY-STALE-READS` subquery reads that a retry does not repeat | 2 of 2 configurations | 3 | durability, list-append |
| `MUT-UPDATE-SEES-OWN-WRITES` an UPDATE that revisits the rows it wrote | 0 of 8 configurations | none |  |
| `MUT-DISK-CACHE-UNVERIFIED` a disk cache that serves damaged files | 12 of 12 configurations | 1 | cache integrity |
| `MUT-DISK-CACHE-SERVE-CUT-READ` a disk cache that serves a read that an eviction cut short | 0 of 0 configurations | none |  |
| `MUT-SEGMENT-UNCHECKED` blocks of segments read without their checksum | 12 of 12 configurations | 1 | bank, cache integrity, damaged reads, durability, index consistency, list-append, workload invariants |
| `MUT-FILTER-OMITS-KEYS` key filters that leave out keys | 12 of 12 configurations | 1 | bank, durability, final read, foreign key, index consistency, list-append, unique, workload invariants |
| `MUT-FILTER-UNCHECKED` filter blocks read without their checksum | 10 of 10 configurations | 1 | cache integrity |
| `MUT-DISK-CACHE-UNCOUNTED` a disk cache that does not count the files of an earlier process | 12 of 12 configurations | 1 | disk cache bound |
| `MUT-MAINTENANCE-UNRECOVERED` a maintenance step that does not recover a panic | 12 of 12 configurations | 1 | panic |

### `MUT-COMMIT-WITHOUT-CAS`

`engine.Mutations.CommitWithoutCAS` writes the manifest unconditionally, so a commit can overwrite a concurrent one.

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| list-append through the engine, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append, storage |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | detected with seed 12 by storage |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 2 by storage |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, a dropped transfer conserves money, and the bank checker only checks totals; without maintainers, only the storage checker finds the objects of a dropped commit that GC cannot collect, in 2 of the first 100 seeds, the first at seed 80 |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by storage |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, which leaves a consistent state in which no value repeats, the unique workload does not check that acknowledged writes survive, and in 20 seeds no dropped commit leaves the store with objects that GC cannot collect |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | cannot detect: an unconditional manifest write drops whole concurrent commits, which leaves a consistent state in which no value repeats, and the unique workload does not check that acknowledged writes survive; only the storage checker finds the objects of a dropped commit that GC cannot collect, in 11 of the first 100 seeds, the first at seed 21 |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 2 by real-time order |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by real-time order |

Targeted tests:

- `internal/engine` `TestMutations/CommitWithoutCAS_lets_a_stale_commit_overwrite_a_newer_one`: with the mutant, a stale commit overwrites another process's newer commit
- `internal/workload` `TestRun/finds_the_lost_writes_of_a_commit_without_CAS`: the real-store workload's checkers find the lost writes of the mutant

- `internal/engine` `TestMutations/SegmentUnchecked_serves_a_block_whose_bytes_the_store_damaged,_and_keeps_serving_it_from_the_cache`: with the mutant, a block whose value the store damaged is served as a wrong value, and served again from the memory cache after the store returns whole bytes

### `MUT-FILTER-OMITS-KEYS`

`engine.Mutations.FilterOmitsKeys` leaves every other key of a segment out of its key filter, so that a point lookup of such a key skips the segment that holds its newest value and reads an older value, or none.

| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by durability, list-append |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by bank |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by workload invariants, bank |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 2 by durability |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by workload invariants, durability, list-append |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by workload invariants, index consistency, bank |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by workload invariants, index consistency, bank |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by index consistency, unique |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by unique, index consistency |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by foreign key |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by foreign key, final read |

Targeted tests:

- `internal/engine` `TestMutations/FilterOmitsKeys_makes_a_point_lookup_skip_the_segment_with_the_newest_value_of_a_key_it_left_out`: with the mutant, the filter of a segment leaves out its second key, and a point lookup of that key reads the value of an older segment

### `MUT-FILTER-UNCHECKED`

`engine.Mutations.FilterUnchecked` decodes the filter blocks of segments without checking their checksums, and caches what the store returns before decoding it, so that a filter block whose bytes the store damaged is trusted, or cached and trusted later. It runs with damaged reads from the store and with blocks of 128 bytes, so that segments have filter blocks.

| list-append through the engine, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 3 by cache integrity |
| bank through the engine, no maintainers | not applicable: the bank workload through the engine keeps four accounts, whose segments fit in one block even of 128 bytes, so no segment has a filter block |
| bank through the engine, 2 maintainers | not applicable: the bank workload through the engine keeps four accounts, whose segments fit in one block even of 128 bytes, so no segment has a filter block |
| list-append through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 1 by cache integrity |
| list-append through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 10 by cache integrity |
| bank through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 3 by cache integrity |
| bank through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 7 by cache integrity |
| unique through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 2 by cache integrity |
| unique through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by cache integrity |
| foreign-key through SQL, no maintainers | detected with seed 12 by cache integrity |
| foreign-key through SQL, 2 maintainers | detected with seed 1 by cache integrity |

Targeted tests:

### `MUT-DISK-CACHE-UNCOUNTED`

`cache.DiskMutations.UncountedAtOpen` leaves the files that are in a disk cache directory at open out of the cache, so that a restarted process never counts or evicts them and its directory grows past the bound.

### `MUT-MAINTENANCE-UNRECOVERED`

`engine.Mutations.MaintenanceUnrecovered` lets a panic unwind out of a maintenance step instead of recovering it, which in the driver's background goroutine ends the process. It runs with `engine.Mutations.MaintenancePanics`, which makes one in three maintenance steps that get to work panic in the middle of a compaction or a GC pass, and with the clients' maintenance coordinated by the lease, so that the panic reaches the client's task, which fails the run.

## Reached states

The fixed simulator corpus must reach every state at least once, or its test fails. The counts of each run are in the CI report.

| ID | State | Antithesis assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `STATE-LOST-ACK-LANDED` | a manifest write whose answer was lost is resolved as landed | "a lost manifest write is found to have landed" |
| `STATE-LOST-ACK-CONFLICT` | a manifest write without a definite answer, from a lost acknowledgement or a failed request, is resolved as a conflict, because another commit took its sequence number | "a lost manifest write is found to have lost to a concurrent commit" |
| `STATE-LIVE-UNKNOWN` | a commit outcome is unknown in a client process that did not crash | "a commit outcome is unknown in a process that keeps running" |
| `STATE-AUTOCOMMIT-RETRY` | an autocommit statement retries after a conflict | "an autocommit statement retries after a conflict" |
| `STATE-COMPACTION-REBASE` | a compaction reapplies its swap on top of commits that landed meanwhile | "a compaction rebases on commits that only added segments" |
| `STATE-COMPACTION-PARTIAL-REBASE` | a compaction that left the oldest or the newest segments alone reapplies its swap on top of commits that landed meanwhile, which go after the segments it left alone | "a compaction that left some segments alone rebases on newer commits" |
| `STATE-COMPACTION-KEEPS-TOMBSTONE` | a merge of segments that excludes the oldest one keeps a tombstone, because an older segment may still hold the key | "a compaction that excludes the oldest segment keeps a tombstone" |
| `STATE-COMPACTION-UPPER-TIER` | a tiered compaction merges segments of tier 2 or higher, which earlier merges made | "a compaction merges segments of tier 2 or higher" |
| `STATE-COMPACTION-WINDOWS` | one compaction merges several separate windows of adjacent segments, and swaps them all in one manifest write | "a compaction merges several windows of segments at once" |
| `STATE-GC-REBASE` | a GC pass reapplies its manifest change on top of commits that landed meanwhile | "a GC pass rebases on commits that landed meanwhile" |
| `STATE-GC-KEEPS-LIVE-GARBAGE` | an expired garbage batch lists a live segment, the output of a compaction that a GC pass stamped as an orphan before the compaction's rebase landed, and GC keeps it | "GC keeps a live segment that an expired garbage batch lists" |
| `STATE-GC-BATCH-REWRITTEN` | a GC pass that rebases writes its garbage batch again, because the chain it was to join changed meanwhile, and the first one becomes an orphan | "a GC pass writes its garbage batch again for another chain" |
| `STATE-GC-CHAIN-DROPPED` | a GC pass deletes the garbage of an expired chain of garbage batches, drops the chain from the manifest, and then deletes its batch objects | "a GC pass drops an expired chain and deletes its batches" |
| `STATE-LEASE-TAKEOVER` | a maintainer takes over a lease that another holder let expire | "a maintainer takes over an expired lease" |
| `STATE-LEASE-OVERLAP` | two maintainers believe they hold the lease at the same time | "two maintainers believe they hold the lease at once" |
| `STATE-SNAPSHOT-EXPIRED-REFUSED` | a reader older than the grace period is refused with ErrSnapshotExpired | "a reader older than the grace period is told so" |
| `STATE-BLOCK-READ-RETRY-SUCCEEDED` | a block read that failed transiently is retried and then succeeds | "a retried block read succeeds" |
| `STATE-CRASH-MID-COMMIT-RECOVERED` | a client crashes in the middle of a commit, restarts, and commits again | "a client that crashed during a commit recovers and commits" |
| `STATE-CRASH-MID-COMPACTION` | a process crashes in the middle of a compaction | "a process crashes during a compaction" |
| `STATE-CRASH-MID-GC` | a process crashes in the middle of a GC pass | "a process crashes during a GC pass" |
| `STATE-UNIQUE-AFTER-CONFLICT` | an autocommit statement that passed its unique checks loses its commit to a concurrent one, and its retry fails with a unique violation that the concurrent commit causes | "a unique violation occurs only because of a concurrent commit" |
| `STATE-UNIQUE-VALUE-REUSED` | a client inserts a row with a unique value that its own committed UPDATE or DELETE freed | "a unique value that a committed write freed is taken again" |
| `STATE-FK-AFTER-CONFLICT` | an autocommit statement that passed its foreign key checks loses its commit to a concurrent one, and its retry fails with a foreign key violation that the concurrent commit causes | "a foreign key violation occurs only because of a concurrent commit" |
| `STATE-FK-CASCADE-TABLES` | one statement's ON DELETE CASCADE actions delete rows in more than one table | "a cascade deletes rows in more than one table" |
| `STATE-DISK-CACHE-EVICTION` | a client's disk cache evicts its least recently used entries to stay within its bound | "a disk cache evicts to stay within its bound" |
| `STATE-DISK-CACHE-REFUSED` | a client's disk cache refuses a file that a crash damaged or removed, and the read goes to the store | "a disk cache refuses a damaged file" |
| `STATE-DAMAGED-READ-REFUSED` | a read from the store gets damaged bytes of a block, the manifest, or a garbage batch, and fails with ErrCorrupt instead of serving or caching them | "a read of damaged bytes from the store fails with ErrCorrupt" |
| `STATE-FILTER-SKIP` | a point lookup skips a segment whose key range holds the key, because the segment's key filter does not hold it | "a point lookup skips a segment whose filter does not hold the key" |
| `STATE-FILTER-BLOCK-READ` | a point lookup with neither the root block nor the filter block of a segment in a cache reads both in one range read, and checks each | "a point lookup reads a filter block with its root block" |

Verified by:

- `internal/sim` `TestSimulator/corpus_finds_no_anomalies`: the fixed corpus reaches every declared state at least once, among them crashes during commits, compactions, and GC passes, lost acknowledgements resolved both ways, unique and foreign key violations that only a concurrent commit causes, disk caches that evict and refuse damaged files, damaged reads from the store refused with ErrCorrupt, and point lookups that skip segments by their key filters and read filter blocks with root blocks
